text: If $\lim _{x\to 1}\frac{x^{2}-ax+b}{x-1}=5$, then a + b is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 1}\frac{x^{2}-ax+b}{x-1}=5$

$\Rightarrow$ $(1)^{2}-a(1)+b=0$

$\Rightarrow1-a+b=0$

$\Rightarrowa-b=1......(1)$

Now 'L' hospital rule

2x - a = 5

$\Rightarrow$2 - a = 5 ($\because$ x = 1)

$\Rightarrow$ a = - 3

By putting a = -3 in (1)

$\Rightarrow$ b = -4

$\therefore$ a + b = -7
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
The number of real roots of the equation

 $5 + |2^{x}$
$– 1| = 2^{x}$
$(2^{x}$
– 2) is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When $2^{x}$ $\geq$ 1 

$5 + 2^{x} –1 = 2^{x} (2^{x} – 2)$ 

Let $2^{x} = t$ 

$\Rightarrow$5 + t – 1 = t (t – 2) 

$\Rightarrow$ t = 4, – 1(rejected) 

$\Rightarrow$ $2^{x} = 4$ 

$\Rightarrow$ x = 2 

Now when $2^{x} < 1$ 

$5 + 1 – 2^{x} = 2^{x} (2^{x} – 2)$

Let $2^{x} = t$ 

$\Rightarrow$ 5 + 1 – t = t (t – 2) 

$\Rightarrow$ $0 = t^{2} – t – 6$ 

$\Rightarrow$ 0 = (t – 3) (t + 2) 

$\Rightarrow$ t = 3, – 2 

$2^{x} = 3 ($rejected as $2^{x} < 1), 2^{x} = – 2 ($rejected)

$\therefore$ Only one real root.

text:
Minimum number of times a fair coin must be tossed so that the probability of getting at least one head is
more than 99% is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The probability of no head in $n$ tosses is $\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )^{n}$, so the probability of at least one head is $1-\dfrac{1}{2^{n}}$.

$1-\dfrac{1}{2^{n}}>\dfrac{99}{100}\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2^{n}}<\dfrac{1}{100}\Rightarrow 2^{n}>100$

Since $2^{6}=64<100$ and $2^{7}=128>100$, the least such $n$ is $7$; for $n=6$ the probability is only $1-\dfrac{1}{64}\approx 0.984<0.99$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text: The smallest natural number n, such that the coefficient of x in the expansion of $\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right )^{n}$ is $^{n}C_{23}$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
General term

$T_{r+1}={}^{n}C_{r}x^{2n-2r}.x^{-3r}$

$\therefore$ $2n-5r=1\Rightarrow 2n=5r+1$

$\therefore$ $r=\frac{2n-1}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ Coefficient of x = ${}^{n}C_{\left (\frac{2n-1}{5}\right )}={}^{n}C_{23}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2n-1}{5}=23orn-\left (\frac{2n-1}{5}\right )=23$

$\Rightarrow$ 2n - 1 = 115 $\Rightarrow$ n = 58

 and n = 38

$\therefore$ smallest n = 38

text:
Let $a$, b and c be in G.P. with common ratio r, where $a$ $\neq$ 0 and 0 < r $\leq$ $\frac{1}{2}$
. If 3$a$, 7b and 15c are the first three
terms of an A.P., then the $4^{th}$ term of this A.P. is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
a = a, b = ar and $c = ar^{2}$

3a, 7b, 15c $\to$ A.P.

14b = 3a + 15c

$14(ar) = 3a + 15(ar^{2})$

$15r^{2} – 14r + 3 = 0$

$\Rightarrow r=\frac{1}{3},\frac{3}{5}(rejected)$

Common difference = 7b – 3a

= 7ar – 3a

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{7a}{3}-3a=-\frac{2}{3}a$

$4^{th}$ term is $\Rightarrow$ $15c-\frac{2}{3}a=\frac{15}{9}a-\frac{2}{3}a=a$

text: If $\int x^{5}e^{-x^{2}}dx=g(x)e^{-x^{2}}+c$,  where c is a constant of integration, then $g$(–1) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $x^{2} = t$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\int t^{2}e^{-t}dt$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\left [-t^{2}e^{-t}+\int 2te^{-t}dt\right ]$

$\Rightarrow \frac{-t^{2}e^{-t}}{2}-te^{-t}-e^{-t}$

$\Rightarrow \left (-\frac{x^{4}}{2}-x^{2}-1\right )e^{-x^{2}}+c$

Then $g(x)=-\frac{x^{4}}{2}-x^{2}-1$

$\Rightarrow g(-1)=-\frac{1}{2}-1-1$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{5}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation,

$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=2x+x^{2}\tan x$, $x\in \left (-\frac{π}{2},\frac{π}{2}\right )$,  such that
y(0) = 1. Then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+y(\tan x)=2x+x^{2}\tan x$

I.F. = $e^{\int \tan xdx}$ = $e^{\ln \sec x}$ = sec x

y. sec x = $\int (2x+x^{2}\tan x)\sec xdx$

$\Rightarrow y\sec x=x^{2}\sec x+λ$

$\Rightarrow$ y(0) = 0 + $λ$ = 1 $\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $y = x^{2} + \cos  x$

$\Rightarrow$ y' = 2x – sinx

$\Rightarrow y^{'}\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{π}{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow y^{'}\left (-\frac{π}{4}\right )=-\frac{π}{2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$  $y^{'}\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )-y^{'}\left (-\frac{π}{4}\right )=π-\sqrt{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
If both the mean and the standard deviation of 50 observations $x_{1}, x_{2},..., x_{50}$ are equal to 16, then the mean of $(x_{1} – 4)^{2}$
, $(x_{2}– 4)^{2}$
,....., $(x_{50} – 4)^{2}$
 is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$Mean(μ)=\frac{\sum x_{i}}{50}=16$

$\therefore$ $\sum x_{i}=16\times 50$

$S.D.(σ)=\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{50}-(μ)^{2}}=16$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{50}=256\times 2$

Required mean = $\frac{\sum (x_{i}-4)^{2}}{50}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}+16\times 50-8\sum x_{i}}{50}$

$\Rightarrow$ 256 $\times$ 2 + 16 - 8 $\times$ 16

$\Rightarrow$ 400
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}$,......be an A.P. with $a_{6} = 2$. Then the common difference of this A.P., which maximises the
product $a_{1}a_{4}a_{5}$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
first term = a, Common difference = d 

$\therefore$  a + 5d = 2

$a_{1}. a_{4}. a_{5} = a(a + 3d) (a + 4d)$

f(d) = (2 – 5d) (2 – 2d) (2 – d)

$\Rightarrow$ $f^{'}(d)=0\Rightarrow d=\frac{2}{3},\frac{8}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $f^{''}(d)<0atd=\frac{8}{5}$

$\Rightarrow d=\frac{8}{5}$

text:
If $\cos ^{-1}x-\cos ^{-1}\frac{y}{2}=α$,where –1 $\leq$ x $\leq$ 1, – 2 $\leq$ y $\leq$ 2, x $\leq$ $\frac{y}{2}$
, then for all $x, y, 4x^{2}$
– 4xy cos $α$ $+ y^{2}$
 is equal
to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\cos ^{-1}x-\cos ^{-1}\frac{y}{2}=α$

$\Rightarrow \cos \left (\cos ^{-1}x-\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{2}\right )\right )=\cos α$

$\Rightarrow x\frac{y}{2}+\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\sqrt{1-\frac{y^{2}}{4}}=\cos α$

$\left (\cos α-\frac{xy}{2}\right )=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\sqrt{1-\frac{y^{2}}{4}}$

squaring both sides

$x^{2}+\frac{y^{2}}{4}-xy\cos α=1-\cos ^{2}α=\sin ^{2}α$

$\therefore$ $4x^{2}$
– 4xy cos $α$ $+ y^{2} = 4$ $\sin ^{2}α$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot
